tasks.short: Agree the subject with the editor, gather notes and sources, outline, draft the article, make pictures, revise after comments and hand it in.

steps.what: Teacher agrees the designated subject, audience and length with the editor
Teacher gathers own teaching notes and sources on the subject
Teacher outlines the steps and points the article will cover
Teacher writes the full draft of the instructional articles

loop.input: The teacher's outline, teaching notes and the source passages the teacher chose, plus the publication's style and length limits.
loop.output: A first draft that follows the outline in the publication's style.
loop.check: Code highlights every sentence that cannot be traced to a line in the notes or a chosen source passage and checks the word count; the teacher rewrites or removes each highlighted sentence and rewrites the whole in their own voice.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft; then the teacher writes from the outline.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning an outline and notes into readable prose is writing work no template can do.

steps.what: Teacher makes step-by-step photos or drawings
Editor reviews the draft and sends comments
Teacher revises the article after the editor's comments and hands it in

tasks.design: The teacher keeps the subject, sources and outline; a bounded step turns the outline and the teacher's own notes into a first draft in the publication's style, and code highlights any sentence not traceable to the notes or chosen sources. The teacher rewrites in their own voice, makes the pictures and handles the editor's comments; the editor still reviews.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing the first draft from an outline took most of the time.
tasks.enabler_now: Course and lesson tools turn documents and notes into first drafts and summaries.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add plausible but wrong steps; the teacher's voice and expertise must carry the article.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing where beginners always go wrong and saying it plainly.

ambition.what: Articles written for each new course topic instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The teacher edits and corrects instead of drafting; the editor's role is unchanged.

reach.learn: Whether the traceability check suits short texts.

evidence.claim: A Dutch course tool turns documents or slide decks into a first course draft.
A Dutch lesson editor's AI rewrites text at another difficulty and summarises it.
AI-generated text published to inform the public must be labelled unless a person reviews it and holds editorial responsibility.

assumptions: Boundary: from the editor's request to the final article handed in; publication is outside.
Input contract: style and length limits from the editor; notes and sources chosen by the teacher; fallback is writing from the outline.
Editor time is outside the teacher's savings.
The teacher keeps editorial responsibility for every sentence.
unknowns: How many articles the teacher writes a year.
Whether the publication accepts AI-assisted drafts.
research_questions: How many highlighted sentences does a typical draft contain?

already_counted.description: Teacher rewrites highlighted sentences and the draft's voice.

incremental.description: Teacher puts notes in a form the draft step can trace.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Teachers who write fluently or whose editors reject AI-assisted drafts save little.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The self-enrichment teacher keeps the subject knowledge and voice; first drafts come faster.
skills_to_grow: Editing drafts for accuracy and voice
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who turns each course into a short guide that students can keep.
